## Emerald 2.2.0

Emerald 2.2 adds complete application theming, broader Markdown image support,
heading-aware wiki links, multilingual spell checking, safer standalone-file
windows, and smarter restoration of each vault. These are all user-facing
changes made since the 2.1.0 release.

### Appearance and editor
- Added built-in **Dark** and **Light** themes. Native widgets, painted Markdown,
  Read Mode, callouts, math, images, and Graph View now share the active palette.
- Added a custom theme workshop with named themes, live note previews, direct
  color entry, a color picker, and hue, saturation, and lightness controls.
- Added a persistent **Full width** editor option alongside the existing fixed
  reading-column width.
- Added file-tree ordering by name in either direction or modification time,
  with modified-time trees updating after saves and external changes.
- Kept scroll-past-end available after document and viewport changes so the last
  line can always be moved into a comfortable editing position.
- Enlarged the hold-to-view keyboard shortcut reference.
- Fixed transparent combo-box popups and prevented the mouse wheel from
  accidentally changing unfocused settings controls.

### Markdown, images, search, and links
- Added first-class parsing and rendering for inline, full-reference,
  collapsed-reference, and shortcut-reference Markdown images, plus Obsidian
  image embeds. Optional titles and width/height hints are preserved, reference
  definitions stay out of Read Mode, and image syntax is excluded from spelling.
- Improved image previews in Edit and Read Mode, including responsive sizing,
  stable selection geometry, bounded missing-image cards, and consistent local
  path security checks.
- Added HTML author comments. `<!-- ... -->` remains subdued and editable in
  Edit Mode but is omitted from Read Mode, search, spelling, Graph View, Quick
  Jump, broken-link checks, and link rewrites. Comment markers inside code or
  math remain literal.
- Added `[[Note#Heading]]` and `[[#Heading]]` navigation. Wiki-link completion
  now offers headings after `#`, while heading matching ignores fenced code and
  author comments.
- Extended Find in Note to search inside rendered Read Mode code blocks and
  visibly highlight the active code match. Ordinary editor matches are centered
  in the viewport.
- Removed raw wiki targets from rendered-link hover tooltips.
- Kept link labels visibly struck inside explicit strikethrough and completed
  task text.

### Vaults and files
- Added isolated `.md` and `.markdown` windows through **Open File…**, command-line
  paths, and operating-system **Open with** actions. Standalone documents do not
  scan or index neighboring files and do not replace the remembered vault.
- Standalone windows preserve UTF-8 BOM and line-ending conventions, watch for
  external edits, render existing relative images, and keep vault-only actions
  disabled.
- Emerald now remembers the last open note separately for every vault; a
  configured Home note still takes precedence.
- Closing and reopening Emerald restores the last closed vault instead of the
  vault that happened to be opened most recently during the session.
- The vault switcher is ordered by recent folder activity, using filesystem
  timestamps so the ordering remains meaningful across launches.

### Spelling
- Multiple installed dictionaries can now be active together for multilingual
  notes. Suggestions are interleaved across languages instead of allowing one
  dictionary to fill the entire list.
- Active spelling languages are remembered per vault, including migration from
  the previous single global language setting.
- Replaced the language selector with a persistent checkable menu, making it
  possible to toggle several dictionaries without reopening the menu while
  ensuring at least one language remains selected.

### Updates, packaging, and maintenance
- Bundled versioned release notes in the application. After an upgrade Emerald
  shows **What's New** once, and the same notes remain available from the gear
  menu.
- Added a Windows installer alongside the portable ZIP. The installer registers
  Emerald as an available editor for `.md` and `.markdown` files without forcing
  it to become the default application.
- Added Linux desktop integration and expanded macOS document metadata for
  opening standalone Markdown files.
- Extended core, UI, security, fuzz, and manual release coverage for the new
  Markdown, theme, spelling, vault, navigation, image, and standalone-file paths.
- Updated release automation to install a pinned NSIS toolchain on Windows,
  corrected CPack escaping for installer file associations, and included the
  Markdown-image suite in sanitizer runs.

### Downloads
| Platform | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Linux (x86-64) | `Emerald-x86_64.AppImage` | `chmod +x` and run |
| Linux (ARM64) | `Emerald-aarch64.AppImage` | requires glibc 2.39 or newer |
| macOS (universal) | `Emerald-macOS.dmg` | drag to Applications; first launch **right-click -> Open -> Open** |
| Windows | `Emerald-win64-setup.exe` | installer with Markdown **Open with** registration |
| Windows portable | `Emerald-win64.zip` | extract and run `emerald.exe` |
